findings: Decision: no edit this round. Both files (src/slugs.py, src/ranges.py) at the frozen base already satisfy the spec, so changing them would add risk without benefit.

src/slugs.py slugify: lowers first via title.lower() (so uppercase folds to a-z, not treated as separators), _NON_ALNUM = r"[^a-z0-9]+" collapses each run of non-alnum chars into a single '-', and .strip('-') removes leading/trailing hyphens -- matches spec exactly.
Note on slugify: .strip('-') only trims hyphens; since every non-alnum run was already replaced by '-', any run at the edges becomes '-' and is correctly trimmed, so no stray separators remain.
Non-ASCII input (e.g. 'Café Déjà Vu') correctly folds to 'caf-d-j-vu' because accented letters fall outside [a-z0-9] and become separators, consistent with the spec's explicit a-z/0-9 alphabet.
src/ranges.py clamp: returns lo when value<lo, hi when value>hi, else value -- matches spec (boundary equalities fall through to value).
src/ranges.py in_range: `lo <= value <= hi` matches the required lo<=value<=hi inclusive semantics at both bounds.

Verification approach this round: re-read both files at base, traced every spec clause (lowercase; collapse non-[a-z0-9] runs to single '-'; strip edges; clamp three-way; inclusive range) and confirmed 1:1 match; nothing to patch.
No conflicts with the allowed edit set (src/ranges.py, src/slugs.py) and src/__init__.py is empty as expected.
